absent.note: Absence here is corpus absence, not a claim about the character: a gesture or expression never authored on her line is unobserved, not forbidden.

b2_not_derived.address_terms_for_npcs: Not derivable. The NPC speakers are not in charData.csv, so there is no name form to search her lines for. Only the eight named cast and the protagonist 一悟 have alias forms.
b2_not_derived.expression_label_uncertainty: Expression triggers inherit the C4 hypothesis: a label on a line is the merged visual/context guess, not ground truth.

rhetorical_mechanisms_deferred_to_b3: This list is the B2 residue, kept for provenance. B3 addressed it: see the `mechanisms` section. The B2 residue named deflects a topic, changes the subject, teases, jokes, stalls with repetition, or answers a question with a question - none of these carries an authored stage direction.
b2_not_derived.room_definition: The room is every other speaker in her scenes, named cast and NPCs together; the plan leaves this open.
b2_not_derived.tokenizer: The surface battery splits on punctuation (a class-based tokenizer), not morphology, so particles are matched by string suffix against a fixed list and the n-grams are character n-grams.
b2_not_derived.trigger_causality: Every trigger table is co-occurrence over her lines, not cause. The authored direction is a staging choice on the line; it does not say why.

emotional_pressures.note: Authored @emotion overlay types and C4 expression labels are distinct sets; the first is the author's, the second a hypothesis.

receipts.text: 「一悟……ううっ、一悟……わたしを許してね……」

「本当に、いいのに……」
「うう……一悟……早く帰ってきてね……」

「あう」

「アリス会長へのお願いごと、決まったってことだよね！」
「えっ？」
「わーっ！？　それは絶対駄目！ギルティ！！」
「えへへへへへへ…………」
「え、えへへぇ……ありがと。大好きぃ……」
「そのおやつ、全部うちの部のなの？　やったっ」
「本当！？　どんな話書くの？」
「三ページ解いたら口移しだね！　えへへっ、やる気でてきた！」
「じゃあ放課後は、わたしと一悟の二人きりなんだ！ふっふっふ、下剋上だね」
「えへへ、そうだよ。だって本当のことでしょう？」
「『帰りにポテチを買ってやるから』だって……ふふふ」
「えへへぇ、ほらね千奈。うらやましいでしょー？」
「えへへ……一悟のそんな照れ方、初めて見たから、それに免じて行ってあげる」
「おいしそう……だけど、野菜多いね」
「もっと早く言って……」
「わ、わたしの歌声に問題があるって言いたいの？」
「どうして、そんなに……わたしの演技は、一悟にしか向けてこなかったはずなのに……」
「あ、ごはんできてたんだ。遅れてごめんね」
「どれどれ……」
生暖かい視線に気付いて、急いで顔を引き締める。
部室に飛び込んできた二人は、わたしのことを心配してくれたのかな？
分かっていたけど、榎本先生って……めんどくさい。若干。
「あー、それっ、それだよ！」
「本当？」
「よいしょ、っと」
「あう」
「ううう……」
「うー……一悟、みんなに優しいんだから……」
「ね、一悟？　一緒にごろごろしてようよ」
「えへへ……おんぶしてくれるなら、行くしかないね。仕方ないなぁ」
「……うん、大丈夫なはず。最適サイズはＣカップだって聞いたことあるし……」
「今朝、昔の夢見たの。だから外、出たくない」
「……柔らかさが足りないからじゃないよね？」
「エンターテイメントのためなら誰にでも見せるとか、良くない」
「ちゅっ……れるっ……んっ……ちゅぅっ……」
「んっ……ふふふ……ちゅぅっ……ちゅっ……一悟の、ファーストキスの相手も……わたし、だから……ちゅっ」
「んっ……ちゅっ……んん……ちゅぅ……っ」
「ふわっ！？　ちがっ、違います！　違うから離れてっ」
「って、ああっ！？　もしかして千奈、やっぱり一悟のこと寝取ろうと……！？」
「うううっ、い、一悟っ！」
「今日のところは見逃してあげるけど、隠しごとばっかりは駄目なんだからね」
「えー、どうして？　テストの開放感に任せて、このままさぁ……」
「キス、応えてくれた……えへへ、嬉しい。彼女を求めてくれてるってことだよね？」
「朝から一悟を誘惑していいのは、わたしだけなの！」
「い、一悟になにしてるの！？」
「一悟っ」
「うーん、おやつ食べてたら眠くなってきたなぁ……」
「ふぁぁ……」
「はぁ、はぁっ……い、一悟……あのね……」
「一悟に……は……早く、伝えたいことがあって、百花ちゃんたちに、送ってもらった、の……」
「はあぁあぁ……ぅぅ、も、もぉ……生徒会長の犬めぇ……」
「んぅっ……一悟？」
「むぅぅぅう！　一悟まで半笑いになってる！ばかばかばか！！」
「にゃっ！？」
「ええええっ！？　ななな、なんで！？」
「ぐー、ぐー。なんの準備？」
「ぐー、ぐー。すやすや……」
「もっと早く言って……」
「ど、どう？　一悟」

mechanisms.class_note: Every mechanism is classed `hers` by this reading: each was found by contrasting her spoken lines with the other named speakers' in her scenes (tools/koikano/b3/mayu.py), and the distinctive flag is that contrast on the whole build, not the held-out gate. The class was not checked against the corpus ownership markers. The one move at or under the control share (stammers_first_sound) is kept as `weak`: the script's other speakers stammer as much, so it is house style.
mechanisms.control_definition: The other named heroines' spoken lines in her scenes (the room minus the protagonist 一悟 and minus her). control_rate is hits over that set; it is the per-bible house-style baseline. The B4 gate used a held-out, same-scene contrast with six heroines and is the authority for `distinctive`.
mechanisms.cross_reference: These are the moves that carry no `@emotion` / `@face` / `@action`. The surface rules they lean on are measured separately in `speech_guide` (first-person わたし, the ん hum, えへへ, the `？` / `…` marks) and in `voice.surface`; this section adds the move, not the mark.

mechanisms.definition: Ends a claim or a complaint on だもん / ないもん / たもん, the pouting 'because it is so' of a childhood friend.
mechanisms.method: regex: the line ends (before the final marks) on もん after だ, ん, い, た, る or の.
mechanisms.name: Justifies herself with a sentence-final もん
mechanisms.note: The most separated move she has. The other speakers in her scenes almost never close a line this way.

mechanisms.definition: Starts the line on だって and gives the reason she did or wants something, usually followed by a もん ending.
mechanisms.method: regex: the line starts with だって.
mechanisms.name: Opens a reason with だって
mechanisms.note: A reproach she gives as an explanation, to 一悟 mostly.

mechanisms.definition: Covers pleasure or embarrassment with a written えへ / えへへ / えへへぇ before going on.
mechanisms.name: Laughs the えへへ
mechanisms.note: Written laugh, one beat, then the sentence. Includes the drawn-out えへへぇ.

mechanisms.definition: Builds a sentence of わたし plus a case particle and 一悟 within a few characters (わたしも一悟に..., わたしが一悟を...), stating where she stands with him.
mechanisms.method: regex: わたし, a case particle, up to three characters, then 一悟.
mechanisms.name: Puts herself next to 一悟 in one sentence
mechanisms.note: Her own self-reference form is a surface rule in speech_guide; this is the move of ranking herself against him (and against 千奈 and 百花ちゃん in the same breath).

mechanisms.note: An address habit tied to one person, kept as a mechanism because no one else in her scenes uses that form.

mechanisms.definition: Volunteers the favour with てあげる / であげる (ご奉仕してあげる, 支えてあげられる), the caring-for-him stance.
mechanisms.method: regex: contains てあげ or であげ.
mechanisms.name: Offers to do it for him
mechanisms.note: Others use the form too (the control share is not zero), she uses it about four times as often.

mechanisms.definition: Ends a question or a rebuke by calling his name last (どうしたの、一悟？ / 一悟ぉ).
mechanisms.method: regex: the line ends on 一悟, with optional drawn vowel and final marks.
mechanisms.name: Closes the line on 一悟
mechanisms.note: The vocative sits at the end, so the line is aimed at him before it is heard.

mechanisms.name: Rebuts with ないよ / じゃないよ
mechanisms.note: Mostly the jealous scenes with 一悟, quoting his words back at him.

provenance.b3_reading: B3 added the `mechanisms` section: the recurring rhetorical moves that carry no authored stage direction. The definitions, the class and the tier are the builder's reading; the line counts come from the fixed matchers named per mechanism, and the receipts are real record ids. No API call was made.
corrections: B1 read the alias table from charData.csv, which omits the protagonist 一悟; B2 adds him for the address-term derivation in this bible only.

B3 is a reading, not a measurement: the mechanism list is this builder's judgement of what shapes her speech, so class and tier are interpretive even where the count is mechanical. The B2 residue named 'deflects a topic, changes the subject, teases, jokes, stalls with repetition, or answers a question with a question'; those are covered by `doubles_a_key_word`, `closes_a_turn_with_a_short_question`, `names_a_blow_with_a_loanword` and `plays_a_role_with_stock_catchphrases`.

speech_guide.note: Each rule carries a class (hers / the author's / a moment), a tier (firm / thin / weak, set by one count rule: firm n>=40, thin 10-39, weak under 10, inferred evidence capped at thin; tier_basis states n, tier_was the builder's old value) and an evidence flag (measured / inferred). It also carries `register`: `all` for both H and non-H, `H` or `non-H` where the rule holds in one register only, and `per-register` where the value differs and both are stated. Every rule carries a receipt of counts and, where small, example lines. Trigger statements are co-occurrence, not cause.
